turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `composition` (absorber), `architecture` (n-i-p =
regular, p-i-n = inverted), `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode),
`etl` (electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Each row is a device
CONFIGURATION whose efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently
fabricated cells, so it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single
champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_open_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_open_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
High-PCE devices in the training set are overwhelmingly lead mixed-cation (FA/MA/Cs) absorbers with a bandgap near 1.5–1.6 eV. Lead-free, Sn-rich, Bi/Ag double-perovskite and wide-gap Br/Cl compositions sit far below because of deep defects, oxidation or a Shockley–Queisser penalty. The same data show that interface recombination, not bulk absorption, is what separates 16 % from >20 % cells: 2D/3D capping, fullerene or NDI SAMs on the oxide, and PTAA/PFN interlayers all raise Voc by suppressing majority-carrier leakage. Contact chemistry follows the same pattern—Au (or MoO3/Ag) on Spiro and Cu (or Ag) on BCP are ohmic and chemically inert, whereas bare Al, acidic PEDOT:PSS or carbon without a mesoporous scaffold limit FF.

Applying those constraints to the pool:

- **c015** (CsFAMAPbBrI|(EPA)PbI, mp-TiO2, Spiro, Au) places a wider-gap 2D layer on the HTL side of the record n-i-p stack. The 2D sheet blocks electrons, passivates under-coordinated Pb and is the motif behind the 22.9 % and 19.7 % training champions.
- **c085** (CsFAMAPbBrI, C60|BCP, PTAA|PFN-Br, Cu) is the canonical inverted architecture. PTAA HOMO alignment plus PFN-Br wetting/passivation, C60/BCP electron selectivity and a diffusion-resistant Cu electrode reproduce the 20.1 % training cell with an extra recombination-reducing interlayer.
- **c093** is the same inverted stack with PCBM|BCP/PTAA/Ag—the exact layer sequence that already delivered 20.3 % in training (only the extra C60 layer is missing).
- **c036** (NDI:SnO2-np, Spiro, Au) uses SnO2 (superior CB alignment and fewer deep traps than TiO2) mixed with an electron-deficient NDI that passivates oxide vacancies, analogous to the ImAcHcl- and PEG-modified SnO2-np cells at 20.3 % and 19.8 %.
- **c092** (FAMAPbI, SnO2-np, Spiro, MoO3|Ag, sequential spin) combines the nanoparticle ETL that appears in the 22 % and 20.2 % cells, a double-deposition process that densifies the absorber, and a MoO3 buffer that makes Ag ohmic while blocking metal diffusion (19.5–19.6 % analogues).

All five therefore combine an optimal-gap, phase-stable absorber with selective, low-recombination contacts and a process known to yield compact, low-defect films.

Final: c015, c085, c093, c036, c092
